title: Assessment
description: A structured evaluation of a claim's evidential support. An assessment records three SEPARATE dimensions: (1) conclusion — the assessed direction of the evidence; (2) confidence — the epistemic strength of that conclusion; (3) dispute_status — whether the assessment is under active formal challenge. These are deliberately not conflated: an assessment can be high-confidence and disputed, or low-confidence and undisputed.

id.description: Stable entity identifier in format boe:assessment:<ulid>. Constant across versions.

rationale.description: Written explanation of the conclusion and confidence level. Must describe: what evidence was weighed, why it supports this conclusion at this confidence, what contrary evidence exists, and what new evidence would change the assessment.

link_ids.description: The ClaimEvidenceLink entities considered in this assessment. Links carry polarity, so supporting and contradicting evidence are both captured here — an assessment that omits known contradicting links is methodologically invalid.

confidence_factors.description: Structured assessment of the individual confidence factors from the methodology.

evidence_strength.description: Whether evidence is direct or circumstantial, first-hand or reported.

corroboration.description: Whether multiple independent sources corroborate the claim.

completeness.description: Whether the evidence base is reasonably complete.

context_integrity.description: Whether evidence is being interpreted in proper context.

what_would_change_assessment.description: Explicit statement of what new evidence or information would change this conclusion or confidence level.

methodology_version.description: The version of METHODOLOGY.md this assessment was made under (e.g., '0.2.0').
